name: SyntheticEvent
syntax: function handleClick(event) { ... } // event is a SyntheticEvent
description: React wraps native DOM events in a cross-browser wrapper object called SyntheticEvent, normalizing behavior across browsers while mirroring the native event API.
notes: Since React 17+, synthetic events are attached at the root DOM container rather than document, but the wrapper API itself is unchanged. Access the underlying native event via `event.nativeEvent` if needed.

name: onClick
description: The event handler prop for click events on an element, called with a SyntheticEvent when the user clicks it.
notes: Pass a function reference (or arrow function), not the result of calling it — `onClick={handleClick()}` would invoke it immediately on every render.

name: onChange
description: The event handler prop fired when a form element's value changes, used to keep controlled inputs in sync with state as the user types or selects.
notes: Unlike plain HTML, React's onChange fires on every keystroke (similar to the native `input` event), not just on blur.

name: onSubmit
description: The event handler prop fired when a form is submitted (via a submit button or pressing Enter), commonly paired with preventDefault to stop the native page reload.

name: event.preventDefault()
description: Stops the browser's default action for an event, such as a form submit reloading the page or a link navigating.
notes: Works the same on React's SyntheticEvent as on native events.

name: event.target
description: A property on the event object referencing the DOM element the event actually occurred on, commonly used to read an input's current value.
returns: The DOM element that dispatched the event.
notes: Distinguish from `event.currentTarget`, which is the element the handler is actually attached to (useful when the handler is on a parent).

name: Passing Arguments to Event Handlers
description: Wrapping a handler in an inline arrow function so extra arguments (like an item's id) can be passed along with the event.
notes: Creates a new function on every render; for hot paths combine with useCallback if that matters for a memoized child.

name: Event Delegation in React
description: React attaches a single listener per event type at the root container (or document, pre-React 17) and dispatches events to the right component via its virtual DOM tree, rather than attaching a native listener per element.
notes: This is why `event.stopPropagation()` on a SyntheticEvent doesn't stop a native listener registered outside React from also seeing the event.

name: Inline vs Defined Handlers
description: Handlers can be written inline as arrow functions in JSX, or defined once and referenced by name; the choice affects readability and whether a new function is created each render.
notes: The performance difference is negligible for most components; prioritize readability unless profiling shows re-creating the function actually matters.

name: event.stopPropagation()
description: Prevents an event from continuing to bubble up to ancestor elements' event handlers within React's synthetic event system.
notes: Common pattern for preventing a click inside a modal from also triggering an overlay's 'close on click' handler.
